candidates.source_description:
Baby Waiting For Birth is one of several sculptures of infants in Vigeland Park.
The park is the world’s largest sculpture park made by a single artist, and is one of Norway’s most popular tourist attractions. The park is open to visitors all year round.
The unique sculpture park is Gustav Vigeland’s lifework with more than 200 sculptures in bronze, granite and wrought iron. Vigeland was also in charge of the design and architectural layout of the park. The Vigeland Park was mainly completed between 1939 and 1949.

candidates.attribution: 3D capture by Ørjan Sandland (orjansandland), published on Sketchfab under CC BY 4.0 and distributed unchanged in AllenAI Objaverse. Physical sculpture attributed to Gustav Vigeland; stone carving by Ivar Broe, Nils Jønsson and Karl Kjær.
candidates.scan_source: Photogrammetric capture by Ørjan Sandland (orjansandland) records the granite column and its pedestal at Vigeland Park. The model isolates the monument from the surrounding terrace and separate figure groups.
candidates.note: Intertwined human figures climb and support one another in a densely carved granite column. Vigeland modelled the work in 1924–1925; the stone was carved at the park from 1929 to 1942. The museum’s park chronology credits Ivar Broe, Nils Jønsson and Karl Kjær as the stone carvers. This capture includes the column and its pedestal, while the surrounding plateau and its separate granite groups are outside its scope. The complete captured column-and-pedestal dimensions are unconfirmed; published column measurements are not treated as a physical calibration of this assembly.
candidates.source_description:
The Monolith is the main sculpture in the Vigeland sculpture park in Oslo, Norway. The 17 meter tall column has 121 figures, all carved from a single block of granite. 

* Rendering Software: Reality Capture
* Images: 306 JPG
* Render setting: High quality
* Processing time: 1h29m
* Camera: Phantom 4 Pro, Sony A7R2

Getting access to this monument without being disturbed is extremely difficult, as it is located in a busy public park. Unfortunately for modeling, my one shot at getting this was a sunny morning at 5am.
